note: Upgrade walkthroughs. One flow per component. The site renders the steps in order for the selected flow, resolves the version placeholders from the version matrix, and lets the operator download a runbook. Order is the contract: a step marked gate must pass before the next one starts.

flows.title: Kubernetes and Kubespray
flows.downtime: Control plane rolls one node at a time. Workloads keep running if PodDisruptionBudgets exist; without them, expect pod restarts.
flows.rollback: None. Kubernetes does not support downgrade. The restore path is the backup taken in step 1.

steps.title: Confirm compatibility and mirror the target artifacts
actions: Target release is in the supported set (five releases, release-2.28 .. release-2.32)
Target Kubernetes minor is exactly one above the current one
Kubelet, kube-proxy, CoreDNS, etcd and the CNI versions are compatible with the target
Every image and binary for the target is mirrored and pull-verified
steps.command: python3 scripts/kubespray_release_matrix.py release-2.28 release-2.29 release-2.30 release-2.31 release-2.32

steps.title: Back up etcd and the cluster state
actions: Snapshot etcd on every control-plane node
Export the current inventory and group vars
Record the current versions for the rollback comparison
steps.command:
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key \
  snapshot save /backup/etcd-$(date +%F-%H%M).db

steps.title: Create the target release's environment
actions: Check out the target Kubespray release into its own directory
Create its own virtualenv with its pinned Ansible
Copy the inventory and re-apply the site group vars
Never reuse the previous release's virtualenv
steps.command:
git -C /opt/kubespray clone --branch release-2.32 --depth 1 \
  https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubespray /opt/kubespray/release-2.32
python3 -m venv /opt/kubespray/venv-release-2.32
/opt/kubespray/venv-release-2.32/bin/pip install -r /opt/kubespray/release-2.32/requirements.txt

steps.title: Run the upgrade playbook
actions: Run cluster.yml from the target release against the existing inventory
Watch the control plane first, then the workers, one node at a time
Stop at the first failed task; do not re-run blindly

steps.title: Validate before moving the next minor
actions: All nodes report the target version and Ready
etcd members are healthy and the leader is stable
CNI and CoreDNS pods are running on the new version
A test workload schedules, pulls an image and answers a request
steps.command:
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl -n kube-system get pods
kubectl -n kube-system exec etcd-<node> -- etcdctl endpoint health --cluster

steps.title: Record the new binding
actions: Update the inventory's kubespray-release marker
Update the version matrix check date
Keep the previous release directory until the next upgrade succeeds

flows.title: Ceph (Rook or cephadm)
flows.downtime: No client downtime if the pools are healthy and one OSD at a time is drained.
flows.rollback: None across a major version. Downgrade within a minor is unsupported; the restore path is the backup.

steps.title: Health and capacity check
actions: ceph status is HEALTH_OK, not HEALTH_WARN
No degraded or backfilling placement groups
At least 25% free capacity in every pool
The Rook release supports the target Ceph version
steps.command:
ceph -s
ceph df
ceph osd tree

steps.title: Back up the cluster configuration
actions: Export the CRUSH map
Export the auth database
Snapshot the monitors' store (or the Rook config ConfigMap)
steps.command:
ceph osd getcrushmap -o /backup/crushmap.bin
ceph auth export -o /backup/auth.keyring
ceph config dump > /backup/ceph-config.json

steps.title: Upgrade the orchestrator first
actions: Rook: upgrade the operator, then CephCluster.spec.cephVersion
cephadm: run ceph orch upgrade start --ceph-version <target>
One daemon type at a time; wait for HEALTH_OK between types
steps.command:
helm upgrade rook-ceph rook-release/rook-ceph -n rook-ceph \
  --version {{version.rook}} -f values.yaml
kubectl -n rook-ceph patch cephcluster rook-ceph --type merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"cephVersion":{"image":"{{value.registryHost}}/ceph/ceph:{{version.ceph}}"}}}'

steps.title: Watch the daemons converge
actions: MONs first, then MGR, MDS, RGW, then OSDs
Do not start a second upgrade while a daemon is still restarting
Confirm each type reaches HEALTH_OK before the next
steps.command:
ceph orch ps --daemon-type mon
ceph orch ps --daemon-type osd
watch -n 10 ceph -s

steps.title: Prove the data path works
actions: Write and read a test object through RGW
Mount a CephFS volume and read a file
Create a PVC and confirm it binds
Run a CSI snapshot and restore
steps.command:
rados -p rbd bench 10 write --no-cleanup
kubectl -n {{value.appNamespace}} get pvc

flows.title: Istio
flows.downtime: No data-plane downtime with a revision-based canary. Sidecar mode restarts pods as namespaces move.
flows.rollback: Available only while the old revision is installed: move the namespace label back. No downgrade.

steps.title: Confirm the version window and mirror the images
actions: Target minor is one above the current one
The Kubernetes minor is inside the target Istio's support window
Every image for the new revision is mirrored
steps.command:
istioctl version
istioctl manifest generate --revision {{revision}} -f istio-operator.yaml | grep -E 'image: '

steps.title: Install the new revision alongside the old one
actions: Install with a revision name derived from the version
Both control planes run simultaneously
Do not remove the old revision yet
steps.command:
istioctl install --revision={{revision}} -f istio-operator.yaml
kubectl -n istio-system get pods -l istio.io/rev={{revision}}

steps.title: Move namespaces one at a time
actions: Change the injection label to the new revision
Restart the workloads in that namespace only
Watch error rate and latency for one business cycle before the next namespace
steps.command:
kubectl label namespace {{value.appNamespace}} istio.io/rev={{revision}} --overwrite
kubectl rollout restart deployment -n {{value.appNamespace}}

steps.title: Prove mTLS and policy still apply
actions: istioctl analyze reports no errors
A negative authorization test is still denied
Proxy version matches the new revision
steps.command:
istioctl analyze -A
istioctl proxy-status

steps.title: Remove the old revision
actions: Only after every namespace has moved
Keep the old IstioOperator file in Git for reference
Record the new revision in the upgrade log
steps.command: istioctl uninstall --revision=<old-revision>

flows.title: Edge load balancer
flows.downtime: None if the VIP moves cleanly. One node at a time, draining first.
flows.rollback: Revert the image tag in the Compose file and recreate the stack on the same node.

steps.title: Confirm the standby can hold the VIP
actions: VRRP state on both nodes is BACKUP/MASTER as expected
Health checks are passing on both
The target image is mirrored and pullable

steps.title: Move traffic off one node
actions: Lower the VRRP priority or stop keepalived on the node being upgraded
Confirm the VIP moved and sessions drained
Upgrade the node that no longer holds the VIP
steps.command:
systemctl stop keepalived
ip -br addr show | grep {{value.edgeVip}} || echo 'VIP moved'

steps.title: Update the stack on that node
actions: Update the image tags in the Compose file
docker compose pull, then up -d
Confirm the health endpoint answers locally
steps.command:
cd /opt/edge && docker compose pull && docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://{{value.edgeVip}}/healthz

steps.title: Fail back and upgrade the second node
actions: Start keepalived on the first node and confirm it takes the VIP back
Repeat steps 2 and 3 on the second node
Both nodes end on the same image tag
steps.command:
systemctl start keepalived
ip -br addr show | grep {{value.edgeVip}}

steps.title: End-to-end check through the VIP
actions: TLS chain is valid through the VIP
Backend health is green in the stats page
VRRP state is stable with no flapping in the logs
steps.command:
curl -sSI https://{{value.edgeVip}}/ | head -3
journalctl -u keepalived --since '10 min ago' | grep -i state

flows.title: GPU operator, driver and CUDA
flows.downtime: The drained GPU node only. Inference capacity drops while the node is out.
flows.rollback: Reinstall the previous driver and operator versions on the drained node before uncordoning.

steps.title: Check the compatibility chain
actions: Driver branch supports the target CUDA
GPU Operator version supports the driver branch
Every image is mirrored
steps.command:
kubectl get pods -n gpu-operator
nvidia-smi

steps.title: Cordon and drain one GPU node
actions: Cordon the node
Drain with --ignore-daemonsets and --delete-emptydir-data
Confirm no inference pod is still running there
steps.command:
kubectl cordon {{value.nodePrefix}}-gpu-1
kubectl drain {{value.nodePrefix}}-gpu-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data

steps.title: Upgrade the operator, then the driver
actions: Upgrade the operator chart first
Let the operator roll the driver DaemonSet
Do not hand-install a driver on a node the operator manages
steps.command:
helm upgrade gpu-operator nvidia/gpu-operator -n gpu-operator \
  --version {{version.gpu-operator}} -f values.yaml
kubectl -n gpu-operator rollout status ds/nvidia-driver-daemonset

steps.title: Prove the node before uncordoning
actions: nvidia-smi shows the target driver and no Xid errors
A test pod requests a GPU and gets a MIG slice
DCGM metrics report for the node
steps.command:
kubectl uncordon {{value.nodePrefix}}-gpu-1
kubectl run gpu-test --image={{value.registryHost}}/platform/cuda-test --restart=Never --limits=nvidia.com/gpu=1

flows.title: Vault and the PKI
flows.downtime: None in an HA setup: upgrade the standby first, then fail over, then the old active.
flows.rollback: Restore the raft snapshot on the upgraded node. Vault does not support downgrade in place.

steps.title: Snapshot and confirm the unseal path
actions: Take a raft snapshot and verify it opens
Confirm the unseal keys are available offline
Confirm the audit device is writing
steps.command:
vault operator raft snapshot save /backup/vault-$(date +%F).snap
vault operator raft snapshot inspect /backup/vault-$(date +%F).snap

steps.title: Upgrade the standby node
actions: Stop the standby, upgrade the binary or image, start it
Confirm it rejoins as standby and the leader is unchanged
steps.command:
systemctl stop vault && <upgrade> && systemctl start vault
vault operator raft list-peers

steps.title: Step down and upgrade the old active
actions: Step down the active so the upgraded standby takes over
Upgrade the remaining node
Confirm the cluster has one leader and two followers
steps.command:
vault operator step-down
vault status

steps.title: Prove secrets, PKI and auth still work
actions: Read a secret through the Kubernetes auth method
Issue a certificate from the PKI mount
Log in through OIDC if it is enabled
Audit log shows the operations
steps.command:
vault kv get {{value.vaultEngine}}/apps/{{value.appNamespace}}/demo
vault write pki/issue/{{value.appNamespace}} common_name=test.{{value.domain}}

flows.title: Ingress controller portfolio
flows.downtime: None if traffic is migrated per hostname before the old controller is removed.
flows.rollback: Move the hostname back to the previous controller. Both remain installed until the migration is complete.

steps.title: Check the lifecycle stage and the deprecation date
actions: Controller is in Candidate, Supported or Deprecated
No upstream retirement announcement since the last check
The annotation set has a documented migration path
steps.command:
kubectl get ingressclass
kubectl -n <ns> get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=nginx-ingress

steps.title: Install the target controller in parallel
actions: Install with a distinct IngressClass or GatewayClass
Do not claim a hostname that the old controller still serves
Mirror the controller image and the CRDs
steps.command: kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/{{version.kubespray}}/standard-install.yaml

steps.title: Move one hostname at a time
actions: Create the equivalent Ingress or HTTPRoute on the new controller
Switch DNS or the edge upstream for that hostname only
Compare access logs and error rate for one business cycle
steps.command:
kubectl get httproute -A
curl -sSI https://app.{{value.domain}}/ | head -3

steps.title: Remove the old controller after the last hostname moves
actions: Confirm no IngressClass references remain
Remove the old controller and its CRDs
Update the ADR and the lifecycle table
steps.command:
kubectl get ingress -A -o wide
kubectl delete -f <old-controller-manifests>

flows.title: Helm 3 to Helm 4
flows.downtime: None. Helm is a client; the cluster is untouched by the client upgrade.
flows.rollback: Keep the Helm 3 binary and the release secrets. Helm 4 writes its own storage format; do not downgrade a release that Helm 4 already modified.

steps.title: Confirm the deadline and the chart compatibility
actions: Helm 3 security fixes end 2027-02-10
Kubespray release-2.32 ships Helm 3.22.0 internally: do not replace it inside the release venv
Every chart in use is tested under Helm 4
steps.command:
helm version
ls /opt/kubespray/release-2.32/bin/ 2>/dev/null | grep helm

steps.title: Install Helm 4 alongside Helm 3
actions: Install to a different path and name
Alias explicitly; never rely on PATH order for a migration
Argo CD keeps its own rendering path and is unaffected
steps.command:
curl -fsSL {{value.filesRepo}}/get.helm.sh/helm-v4-linux-amd64.tar.gz | tar xz
install -m 0755 linux-amd64/helm /usr/local/bin/helm4

steps.title: Re-run every chart operation under Helm 4
actions: helm4 template for every chart, compare the manifests
helm4 list and helm4 get values in every namespace
Upgrade one non-critical release with helm4 and diff the result
steps.command:
helm4 list -A
helm4 template <release> <chart> -f values.yaml | diff - <(helm template <release> <chart> -f values.yaml)

steps.title: Switch the pipelines and keep Helm 3 until the date
actions: CI images use Helm 4
No release is operated by both binaries
Helm 3 binary stays available for one rollback window
steps.command:
helm4 version
helm4 list -A --all-namespaces | wc -l
